title: Strategies to reduce low-value preoperative testing in low-risk ambulatory surgery: a rapid review for a regional executive committee
abstract: Objective: to identify strategies that reduce low-value preoperative testing in adults having low-risk surgery, the size and durability of their effects, and their effects on same-day cancellations and complications. Methods: rapid review with streamlined screening and extraction, narrative synthesis by strategy type and GRADE certainty per outcome. Results and conclusions will follow the review.
introduction: Routine preoperative tests persist for healthy adults despite guidance. Retrieved studies suggest that changes to ordering systems and feedback on clinicians' own ordering reduce testing, while education alone fades.
methods: Search of three databases and a register from 2010; single screening with 20 percent verification; checked extraction; design-appropriate risk of bias tools; certainty per outcome.
results: No data have been extracted yet. The report will present the study flow, a table by strategy type, an effect direction plot, durability, balancing outcomes and certainty ratings.
discussion: The discussion will translate the findings into options for the committee and state the limits of rapid methods and indirect comparisons.
limitations: Rapid methods; English-language restriction; mostly before-after evidence.
conclusion: To be written after the review; it will rank no strategy beyond what the certainty ratings support.
reportingChecklist: PRISMA 2020 items applicable to rapid reviews
summary: Rapid review draft with results left empty.
